items.text: Hell yeah, even if you are someone that can’t handle gore, this game shows amazing uses of physics in VR. Sliding on the rope with your axe, imagine grabbing each side of a weapon to do the same thing. The climbing up the ledge using your weapon and surroundings is exactly what I can’t wait for in next gen VR.

Simply put, you need to convince the wife to mount to the ceiling or a decently high self above your tv which is what I do. Frankly it’s the best option for any standing game and works just fine with sitting games as long as the chair isn’t too far back. That way you can put nicknacks with the camera making it an appealing shelf to show things off.
You’re in the wrong subreddit bud
Takes one to know one

Well the guy who helped invent internet Explorer has a company developing non-invasive hardware to be able to talk to machines but don’t know if they are also looking into sending info back to the brain. With any truly new tech, there are ways to use it for harm and ways to use it for good. That’s never going to change unless you want to stay the same forever.

items.title: [fluff] What are you excited to do in NMS VR?
items.text:
[fluff] What are you excited to do in NMS VR?
There is so much I can’t wait to experience. I grew up on all of the classic sci-fy books and VR itself blew my mind. Now I’ll have the chance to experience an advanced sci-fy universe as if I’m really there.

Jumping through black holes is going to be insane. Even just standing on planet and looking up as you call in your freighter. Then freaking jumping in your ship and actually flying up to it. The sense of scale from that alone is going to be wild. Not to mention how a planet will just expand and fill your view as you fly towards one and land. So many things, even the simplest, I’m so excited to experience.
That’s what they said about No Man’s Sky ;]

Same here, besides occasional Overwatch with friends and Division 2, there hasn’t really been a game I’ve played that I didn’t think man I wish this was VR. Even RDR2 was fun but meh to me overall and the online isn’t shaping up very well. After NMSVR I won’t be satisfied with another game until the PS5 PSVR2 Starfield or Elders Scrolls 6.
All I can think and say is “I CANT WAIT!”

That’s what I’m saying. It’s going to be awesome stepping through a life size stargate in VR, with no load screens making it even more amazing. If they’re making it possible to grab the throttle and stick in VR then it’s likely we’ll actually push each button on the gate controller and the moment it blasts open when you push the activate stone. Oh man.
Gary, where’s your other hand?
I’ve spent whole trips playing Skyrim VR and Rec Room. It makes Skyrim look more like a game but at the same time feel more real.

When the hell is the bull sh!t forced click turning going to be removed? That’s the thing that prevented me from buying after playing the open beta. It’s horribly difficult to rotate when in a CQC situation. Every time I died was because of having to click, recently, click, resented the damn right stick just to effing turn quickly. Frankly any VR game that has ANY forced blinders or click turning or similar is too far behind already. Do research if you’re going to develope a VR game, very very few of us want anything except smooth turning.

Smooth turning should of been there day one, in fact it should of been there pre-beta. It’s a HUGE fundamental part of maneuvering at all in this game and screws you over again and again in CQC. That fact that you guys are essentially putting such an important feature on the back burner for “future updates” is a joke and makes me lose trust in that you guys are listening to the players.

This is a huge mistake on your guys part if you are able to make it happen but not moving forward with it. The game’s multiplayer is already sparse from what I’ve played and that’s on the weekend Saturday and Sunday nights. If at all possible I highly suggest you get crossplay with PCVR AND PSVR. Without it, the player base will be trash and your game will die a quick death on PSVR. It’s unfortunate because I really enjoy your game. I’ve been dying for a civ or RTS like VR game but it loses fun after awhile with no people to play against.

It’s the internet, of course I have to. It may be rude and crass but it needs to be at this point. Even a AAA dev like Ubisoft apparently needs reminding even though it’s been clear for two years that you are shooting yourself in the foot but not making blinders and click turning optional. Especially when you have to use the DS4 as a tracked controller. You can barely aim very far left or right before the tracking starts to fail, this would instantly be solved with smooth turning. They talk big about using DS4 because that want PSVR to remain competitive yet don’t even properly implement it. I don’t normally blow the handle until it’s been said again and again and it’s past that point for this stuff. Not properly finishing a game like this can easily not only give bad reviews of the game or dev but also the system it’s played on and VR needs to grow, not shrink.

Agreed, I loved this game very much and had a blast but these are blatant middle fingers to those on PSVR while claiming they care about PSVR staying competitive against PCVR. They are showing danger signs we’ve seen from past devs and they don’t even have the excuse of being a small dev team. They are freaking Ubisoft.

Although the article author claims it’ll be on PSVR, Population One’s website doesn’t mention PSVR in the trailer or anywhere on the website. So unless this author has some behind the scenes info, it’s only coming to PCVR...
Yup, Microsoft/Xbox has really dropped the ball on VR and if they don’t truly amaze next gen then they could fall back to third place on console purchases.
It only failed in the 90s because the technology wasn’t good enough yet. It is quite obviously good enough today to run on only hardware let alone up to date hareware like we’ll have on next gen.
I sure hope it’s coming to PSVR, just kinda odd to see their official site have literally nothing at all anywhere even mentioning PSVR.
I’m hoping so, and I agree that NMS going VR will ideally take away most dev’s excuses for not developing for PSVR.

I whole heartedly agree. It’s truly mind blowing and it’s literally only the beginning. I don’t understand the neigh sayers. They seem to either be people who haven’t tried 6DOF VR and are too stubborn to try it or people who are never happy and won’t be satisfied until you literally jack your brain into a computer so their lazy asses can turn into potatos while they play VR. Don’t get me wrong I can’t wait for feed dive VR as long as it’s non-invasive, but that doesn’t mean I’m not going to enjoy the hell out of what we have now.
Absolutely this, Nintendo needs to shut their faces claiming this is VR.

I had hopes literally years ago they had been talking about it but they said they will not be bringing the VR to PSVR because they are pompous. They claim the graphic fidelity is too low for “their” standards. So basically because PSVR can’t run ED at max resolution and quality while in VR, they aren’t even trying to do it. Although that was years ago and NMS is a big eff you to them so one can hope, but I think even if they did at this point, idk if I’d care since I’ll be playing NMS VR.

Well you’re in some luck, I believe light field technology is getting pretty good and could become the new display standard for VR and I believe it achieves 3D without using the bifocal split screen method of today so you’d have just one window or lens to look through.
I agree that could be an issue but could be possibly fixed from simply using larger font or the ability to adjust font size and HUD element size.
This doesn’t activate sneak in game though. Just causes you to squat
VR is the future of gaming, probably all gaming in the next 10 years or less. VR wil become the internet as hardware shrinks and becomes less intrusive so more people are willing to use it.

To clarify, imho, we will still be playing “flat games” but likely we will be in a virtual world with friends or otherwise and playing these flat games there in VR. Or it’ll be an AR/VR combo so you’d still put on glasses to see your flat screen but the same glasses would likely be used for VR. I most certainly could be wrong but I think it’ll be similar to ready player one where the internet will mostly convert to VR.

Copy and pasted my comment:

To clarify, imho, we will still be playing “flat games” but likely we will be in a virtual world with friends or otherwise and playing these flat games there in VR. Or it’ll be an AR/VR combo so you’d still put on glasses to see your flat screen but the same glasses would likely be used for VR. I most certainly could be wrong but I think it’ll be similar to ready player one where the internet will mostly convert to VR.
See my other reply that I posted twice.
See my other reply that I posted twice.
Light field technology negates the need for binocular split screen VR and only requires one view point to still see in 3D and is likely the replacement of current display tech for VR.

See my other comment, but to sum it up, headsets 10 years from now will likely not be much more cumbersome than a pair of glasses. They are likely to be capable of both AR and VR and any flat games could transition to being played while in VR or an AR version of your home/room/etc. Everyone here is thinking of VR as it is now. It’s not going to be anything like it is now in 10 years. With the exponential growth of computers the tech will get smaller and smaller. Your damn smart phone is way more powerful than the Nintendo switch just as an example of current tech doing the same.
Probably won’t happen until PS5 unfortunately

Was Job Simulator out on PCVR or PSVR first? If PSVR then it’s makes you wonder why they changed it this time. Being they’ve released on PSVR before, they should be very familiar with the needed back and fourth with Sony and should of planned for that when planning release dates.

Okay yes that may be true, but the switch is built from the ground up for gaming. So every bit of hardware and free memory is geared towards bringing a better gaming experience. Which I assume would translate to general latency, controller hardware comfort/ease of use/latency, RAM allocated for specifically rendering purposes, etc. A smart phone isn’t designed with only gaming in mind, it’s a jack of all trades while the switch is a gaming machine with the ability to do other things(internet browser, apps, etc). Of course the switch will win, but if a phone was designed from the ground up for gaming as it’s main function, imho, it would beat the switch. My point in my previous comment is still valid as it was simply an example of how fast technology gets smarter and faster. So much so that for example when a new gen console comes out there is a major delay for the software/games made for it to catch up and take true full potential of that hardware. Just look at any game that came out at the launch of a console and then look at a game of similar nature that came out near that consoles end. There are often massive improvements in all aspects including graphics, physics engines, etc. Current example could be No Man’s Sky, the optimization of the software for the hardware it’s running on wasn’t there two years ago but now it is. Something considered impossible two years ago by almost anyone is happening this summer. This increase in tech will only stop when transistors reach a small enough size for quantum mechanics to start messing with the switches and then we can go no smaller and silicon computer technology can get no more complex. We’re still a bit off from that point but it’s closer than you might realize. What the PSVR headset has in it for hardware could very well be shrunk down to something not much bigger or perhaps heavier than a pair of glasses or maybe a hat.
That’s true, only the devs can say for sure I suppose.
If I wasn’t poor I would gold your kindness.
Dugtrio
You’re also talking to a creepy robot

The article in the other post talked about it being some kind of exploration game where the entire ecosystem and environment is simulated in real time and they want you to have the feeling of what it’s like to discover a new land where no human has set foot. See nature in its natural form and be able to interact and influence it.
Sounds awesome, the biggest thing that can sell a VR game is immersion and interactivity.
So if I’m following all of that correctly is the zoo level Phoenix AZ zoo or is it in my eyes?
Okay so this doesn’t show a solution but where we are at this point in deciphering the clues? I mostly followed it fine just wasn’t sure if a final solid answer has been found yet.
Does that mean we can theorize that fires were more likely during the Dino eras? Being there was a ton more oxygen in the atmosphere at the time.
Apparently no one in here has actually been in a black hole in NMS. They are worm holes to a random closer point to the center of the galaxy you’re currently in.

Well admittedly you already need a special drive upgrade to safely go through a black hole in NMS. If you attempt it without the drive you risk major damage to systems and even your ship being destroyed. I should also make note that the black holes are one way worm holes so be wary about going in one unprepared.
For all we know black holes are worm holes. So a black hole acting like what we call a worm hole is no less likely than it being just a super dense planet or a pocket dimension.

Nope, they are guaranteed to bring you 7000 light years +\-1000 light years in a straight line towards the center of the galaxy. There are also hyper black hole that brings you up to distances of 300,000 lights years.
Plus that’s 100s of hours of game play available. Very worth the price.

What time are you on rec room? Because there are often a lot of people online being it’s cross play. You might have the PSVR only check box in settings checked. You’ll want that off so you play with PCVR people as well.

Otherwise, NMS VR is coming this summer. Skyrim VR is well worth the price. So much freedom to play the way you want and progress how you want.

Just my guess but I think it’s supposed to imply that “everybody golfs” in that they show a lot of different people with way different styles and assumed to be different personalities yet they all love to golf.
This is my only complaint so far. How can they not include a multiplayer versus option for a golf game?

Making the next headset compatible with this console would be a major shot in the foot. That’s holding back the potential of the next headset so that it can run on almost 10 year old hardware. I’m not looking to have the same behind the times hardware for another 5 years, I want the next headset to be the best it can be and that means leaving old tech behind. Suck it up and save up, it’s a good two years away, everyone have plenty of time to save.

You’re not looking at the VR tech of the headset apparently because yeah the current headset has visible light tracking that requires very large light designs for it to be easily recognized by the PS4. There’s no eye tracking in the current headset. The display while very good in its own right is already out of date compared to most VR headsets. There’s no mechanics IPD adjustment or similar features. There’s no forward facing camera to allow you to see the real world without taking off the headset which is a major grip with many people today. The list goes on why the current PSVR headset is already falling behind in hardware and thus the ablility to give a more fully immersed experience. What they are doing is saving themselves money in fact making themselves more money because you know everyone will buy the new headset ASAP when it’s out and this headset being backwards compatible likely will convince more to buy now instead of wait and end up buying the next headset anyways. Sony makes bank off both. This is purely a business strategy NOT something that makes sense for the technology.

No, I’m saying using the PSVR headset of today will put you at a disadvantage compared to people using the next headset. Which will likely have things like forward facing camera/s. Better tracking. Eye tracking. Maybe wireless capability. The list can go on. So yeah it’s a bit of a disappointment that the PS5 might be held back even slightly because it has to cater to “old tech”. Just like people using the PS4 Pro suffer today because devs have to cater to the OG PS4’s capabilities.

Dude, the PS5 is likely coming the very end of next year. That alone is a lot of time for tech to be implemented. Frankly if eye tracking isn’t standard then yeah again they are shooting themselves in the foot. Eye tracking is key for FOVed rendering to work and FOVed rendering is the next leap in VR. Eye tracking is old as fuck technology, it’s not something that would be hard to put in the headset.

You’re not making much sense for one being no one is talking about software, we’re all talking about hardware. So you’d jump ship from PSVR because you won’t want to spend the money up front but then would just go spend even more money to get a viable PCVR set up? Again, you make no sense. PS5 is two years away at least, that’s plenty of time to save up maybe a grand total to buy the PS5 and PSVR2 off the bat.
Maybe ironically, the PS5 will be running some form of 8 core AMD chips so at least NMS will work on next gen even better ;p

Cross play between PCVR and PSVR is no problem for Sony. They only care about cross play between Xbox or Nintendo and Sony. Most VR games with multiplayer have cross play with PCVR. Rec Room, Star Trek bridge crew, space junkies, etc. So yeah it’s more likely the devs doing rather than Sony’s.
“Sony wouldn’t publish rubbish” What? There are tons of rubbish games in general on the PlayStation store let alone the PSVR section.
Not true, take away the made up value of a dollar you have been taught to place on everything you see and suddenly it’s not a matter of cost but a matter of equal resource distribution.
No

Hah, you’re not only looking at the world as black and white but also pulling at straws. The world is grey all the way through and that particular form of communism didn’t kill people because of the ideas of communism but because those ruling didn’t follow the actual teachings of communism.

You’re looking at things too black and white. Equal resources wouldn’t mean you get paid a certain amount every such a day but it’d mean that all have equal access to all resources but none can use more than warranted.

That’s still in a system based on money. The only example I can think of a moneyless system would be Star Trek the next generation on Earth money isn’t used. Although I presume that has happened because of replicators and holodecks but on paper at least it’s possible to do it today but would require many people to do jobs without much extra in benefits or since there’s no pay perhaps those that did the “worse” jobs would get a bit more land or something similar that wouldn’t largely set them apart in wealth than others but is still an inventive. I’m not saying I believe this is the way it should be but I’m saying it’s possible but hard to know exactly how since no one is really trying to do so without personal motives which breaks the whole system from the start.

I’m not saying I want communism nor am I exactly supporting it. I am saying that the world could be run on a moneyless system but would require true selflessness and that’s almost impossible with human nature. Almost everyone had personal motives and those ruin the system. Without a new technology to say be able to create food from minimal sources, the ultimate being direct energy to matter conversion, then it’s not likely to happen very easily.

You want the cheapest easiest solution? Buy a pack of dark colored round felt “pads” at Walmart or a similar place. If I’m US they are made by 3M. They have felt on one side and sticky stuff on the other. Just stick a couple together in a stack and stick the stack to the right and left of the lenses and they will act like bumpers for your glasses. Headset too far out? Removes a pad from the stack and try again. Simple and easy to get and replace.

items.title: Next Update
items.text:
Next Update
So I know the devs are busy optimizing for the quest, but this is the third week since the last update. I understand their situation but they’re also losing people by shifting focus so much.

It’s another case of the devs thinking more about new players and less about keeping the players they have. Again, I know they need to make money soon and whatnot but they’re not going to make money if everyone that actually cares about the game leaves. I’m usually on daily but haven’t even played for a few weeks now since the weeklies are repeats for a number of weeks in a row now and there’s no incentive for those that already have it. Plus the lack of any meaningful content for what is becoming months now. We’ve been having a lot of that lately, “updates” that are nothing more than minor patched in features.

The gifting update was not an update, it was a patch to add a feature that is something considered standard in almost any multiplayer game around for a decade now.

I love Rec Room and the devs are generally a cut above the rest but this is getting old. First the focus on screeners over VR, and now more focus on future players over the current.
Shooot, damn I didn’t even realize. Yeah that’s even worse hah.
It could be argued that they need new player because they are catering to future players over current ones.
Yeah I’d rather actual new content than a new version of a current feature at this point.

This is very much my train of thought as well. Rec Room has brought so many experiences and shown how far VR can go and still will. However any game no matter how wonderful or how much charm, especially online games, need added content consistently to maintain a player base. Custom rooms are great so far but are still faaaaaaaaaaar flung from anything like Rec Room originals rooms. Simply because there isn’t enough amazing talent capable of churning out the top tier rooms, and often these rooms require 5-10 people collaborating on them and that spreads the talent even more thin. The tools are there to make amazing rooms but they still require too much talent and practice to use them for Rec Room originals to take a back seat.

Yes, I understand this. However, ideally, there should be a dedicated team for this while there is still a team working on new content. Maybe they simply don’t have enough people, maybe they mismanaged their income. I don’t know, I can’t say for sure because I’m not in the know. So yeah I can’t exactly be mad at them but I will still point out what the genera gaming community expects and even though there are us that will likely come back once an update comes out. There are still many many more that will drop the game, uninstal it, and never come back no matter what’s added.

The whole situation isn’t great for the player base or the devs. It’s unfortunate but it’s the way it is.

Thank you for responding!

As always I hope the best for you guys and this game. I just don’t want it to fail it’s potential. I can easily see it as a staple VR social/game app especially on next gen VR.
Practice makes perfect

Highly likely it’s your lighting conditions. You need to reset the tracking lights for each controller depending on the time of day and colors in the background and so on. So it’s somethjng that needs to be regularly done if tracking starts to get iffy.
What was the point of cross posting this? Obviously this is the kind of person who has brought toxic trash to Rec Room.

Did you try and put it on? Some games will deactivate headset tracking while the headset is off. There is a proximity sensor in the headset between the lenses and above the “nose spot”. Just hold a finger or something close to it so it thinks you have it on so you can check the front if the light is on. Also, I know you said you reset everything but does that mean you also unplugged the power and let cool down the breaker box that the headset connects to? Did you fully shut down your PS4 or just go into standby mode? PSVR seems to regularly glitch if you don’t fully shut down your PS4.


Also, buying a new one would cost around double the price of having Sony fix your current one, assuming it’s even actually broken and isn’t just a glitch.
You don’t need to buy a warranty, Sony has a year long manufacture warranty. They’ll just need the ID number on the headset and a few other things that all should be available to you.
Yeah maybe if it was more than a sentence worth of text lol.
Is it worth the $11.99? I know there are three prisons, does the crafting remain interesting later game?
Are you playing on weekdays or weekends? Being it’s cross play, player base should be okay at least on the weekends.

As someone that was very disappointed with the lack of smooth turning in the beta and said as much, you might of won me over with the quick content and listening and addressing the issues the player base finds.
Unfortunately the same here, I don’t make bank and know I wouldn’t put enough time into the game until VR is added. I’ll just be playing NMS VR until then.

👍🏻

Since you’re here, I’ve noticed more jaggies on PS4 Pro after the recent update. Have smooth lines been reduced on PS4 as part of the optimization or is it a side effect of the added lighting?
Awesome! I’ve been excited to try out the new titan.
The link just goes straight to rec.net?

I’ll be saving up that money for the PS5 instead. I just can’t imagine PS3 processing power worth a few hundred dollars. I assume the quest will still be locked into the oculus store since it doesn’t connect to a PC so less power and still locked content. Might as well save and keep using my PSVR.

Oh yes I will, what’s the point of seeing PS2 graphics better? Oh man I can really see those polygons man. The quest is an expensive toy to me. Yes it will likely bring in lots of VR adopters, but even already owning the PSVR, I don’t find it worth the money for something that will me less than the PSVR in every way except perhaps tracking(although there’s talk about its limitations reaching up, down and behind, this can be worked around on the PSVR but not using the inside out tracking) and the wireless element. I’d rather be wired and have more power and options.
Yes, a working lightsaber. I’ve tried it out and on that level and it’s pretty awesome if you’re a star wars fan especially.

You can smoke every day and not effect your natural dopamine very much as long as you’re not wake and baking every day. Weekdays don’t smoke until you’re home from work and weekend I treat as free reign.

The thing I’m most excited about is of course the “no loading screens” aspect of just taking off and flying out into space is going to be wild. Also, it’ll be the first open world survival game on PSVR and I’m excited to experience a game like that in VR. Especially if you play in hardcore mode(if you die your entire save is deleted) then it really forces you to think and prepare and not take too many risks(almost like real life lol but in space) and I’m excited to see how that feels in VR.

Yes, I noticed the bug the other day and recently. In my dorm every time I placed a specific invention (hypercube decoration) it will despawn after a bit and reappear outside the dorm room and just sit there. Also while working on my custom room, I noticed after scaling and moving some ribbon maker pen objects they force despawned after the intersected another maker pen object while scaling.

Each has their own advantages. Everyone needs to shut it already about this. Teleporters are generally better on flat open terrain and walkers are often better with vertical terrain. Teleporters can squeeze through tiny gaps but walkers can climb and dodge a lot easier.

So it’s really both have their own positives and negatives so learn to change your play style when encountering either.
